comment: Cross-adapter parity contract between @stll/folio-react and @stll/folio-vue. Drives `bun run check:parity-contract`, which parses each adapter's `DocxEditorProps`, `DocxEditorRef`, and nested `PagedEditorRef` from source and applies this contract, failing on any undocumented drift. `paired` = behavior matches between adapters: either both wire the field functionally, or both intentionally no-op it identically. `deferredInVue` = declared in Vue's type surface but not implemented with matching behavior yet. Each deferred entry has a one-line reason. `pairedNotes` records source-verified reasons for non-obvious pairings. Adding a prop or method to either adapter without classifying it here fails the gate.

deferredInVue.accessibleName: React requires an accessible name for its paged editor root; the matching Vue prop and root semantics are deferred.

pairedNotes.outlineDepth: Both adapters apply the shared heading-depth filter, default to two levels, and forward selector changes through onOutlineDepthChange; the host can control and persist the value.
pairedNotes.components: Both wired with the full ten-primitive contract and real defaults. Vue uses monolithic, data-driven primitives where React uses compound parts, while preserving the same host-override capability. DatePickerPopover is consumed by the shared-controller-backed content-control overlay in both adapters; Button renders the Vue dropdown items. Dialog, Select, Menu, Popover, Input, Checkbox, ColorPicker, and OutlineRail remain threaded through their documented chrome consumers.
pairedNotes.featureFlags: Both wired. Each adapter passes the flags with the canonical session's save snapshot to the shared serializeCanonicalSave, which decides between the selective patch and a full repack, and marks the saved package as the session's save baseline (markCanonicalSaved) once the snapshot is still current. Vue threads props.featureFlags into useDocxEditor via a getter and reads it on each save.
pairedNotes.fonts: Both wired. React registers host FontFace entries via paged-editor/hostFonts + a font-ready re-layout. Vue ports the same DOM-only FontFace path (packages/vue/src/utils/hostFonts.ts) and registers on mount / prop change in DocxEditor.vue, then re-measures (resetCanvasContext + clearAllCaches + reLayout), unregistering on change/unmount — mirroring React's hostFonts effect.
pairedNotes.hostShortcuts: Both read the prop once at mount and pass `historyShortcutOwner(hostShortcuts)` to `createStarterKit`, so `"history"` drops the body editor's Mod-z / Mod-y / Mod-Shift-z keymap in both; React also turns off its document-level `useDocumentHistory` key listener. `"print"` makes React's page-level listener pass Cmd/Ctrl+P through untouched; Vue binds no print key, so it is already a no-op there.
pairedNotes.keyboardShortcuts: Both gate their page-level keydown listener on the same core predicate (isKeydownInShortcutScope) against the component root element, with the same default ("document"). The bound key sets differ as they already did: React answers find/replace, print and table deletion (its zoom keys stay with the browser), Vue answers find/replace, hyperlink, File > Open and zoom. React attaches no listener at all under "none"; Vue keeps its window listener and returns on the same predicate.
pairedNotes.marginGuideColor: Both wired with the same painter-level CSS color override and the same default. Runtime changes trigger a repaint in each adapter.
pairedNotes.onCopy: Both wired through the shared hidden-editor manager. The callback fires for a copy DOM event without consuming the browser's clipboard behavior, including in read-only mode.
pairedNotes.onCut: Both wired through the shared hidden-editor manager. The callback fires for editable cut events; read-only cuts are refused through onReadonlyEditAttempt and do not report a completed cut.
pairedNotes.onPaste: Both wired through the shared hidden-editor manager. The callback fires for editable paste events; read-only pastes are refused through onReadonlyEditAttempt and do not report a completed paste.
pairedNotes.onSelectiveSaveTripwire: Both wired. When flags.selectiveSaveTripwire is on, React computes both selective and full buffers and fires onSelectiveSaveTripwire(compareSelectiveVsFull(selective, full)); the comparison is wrapped so it never poisons the save. Vue's save() mirrors this exactly (same tripwire-only full-repack, same compareSelectiveVsFull call, same swallow-on-error guards) and invokes props.onSelectiveSaveTripwire threaded through useDocxEditor. Timing divergence: React fires onSave then the tripwire; Vue fires the tripwire at the end of the core save() (after the bytes are produced) and onSave at the ref-API boundary once save() resolves, so the tripwire fires just before onSave. Both fire only after a successful save and neither blocks it.
pairedNotes.pageRenderer: Both forward the reactive prop into the shared layout pipeline, which selects the page renderer for that layout run. Painting is the only thing swapped: page shells, virtualization and the fingerprint comparison stay shared, so incremental repaint behaves the same under either renderer. Defaults to the existing painter in both adapters.
pairedNotes.preserveDocumentWhileLoading: Both wired. React skips its loading early-return when the flag is set and a document already loaded (`status === 'loading' && (!preserveDocumentWhileLoading || !history.state)`), keeping the prior document mounted. Vue suppresses the loading interstitial when `preserveDocumentWhileLoading && hasRenderedDocumentOnce`; the previous pages stay painted in `pagesRef` (the swap tears down the PM view but does not clear the paint) until the new layout replaces them.
pairedNotes.showHeaderFooterEditing: Both wired, default true. Each adapter gates header/footer double-click entry on this prop, routes input into one persistent ProseMirror view per relationship id, repaints live content and selection geometry from that view, and commits immutable document-model snapshots on close/remove/save. Vue binds the shared core manager directly; React's HiddenHeaderFooterPMs is a thin lifecycle wrapper around the same manager.
pairedNotes.showMarginGuides: Both wired through the shared layout-painter overlay. Each adapter forwards the reactive prop into the shared layout pipeline; every page paints its effective body-content boundary without changing layout or intercepting input.
pairedNotes.showPrintButton: No-op in both. React's classic `Toolbar` component reads this flag, but `DocxEditor` renders `FormattingBar` (not `Toolbar`) and never passes `showPrintButton`; FormattingBar has no print button, so no toolbar print button is rendered regardless of the flag. Vue's Toolbar likewise renders none (print is driven from the menu bar / Cmd+P). Verified: `showPrintButton` appears only in Toolbar.tsx/toolbarPrimitives.tsx (the unmounted classic toolbar), never in DocxEditor.tsx or FormattingBar.tsx.
pairedNotes.showReviewControls: Both wired. React gates its `toolbarPriorityExtra` (a track-changes toggle flipping editing<->suggesting via `toggleTrackChanges`, plus a markup display-mode `StSelect` calling `setDisplayMode`) on this flag; `displayMode` drives the `folio-root--<mode>` root class that the editor.css tracked-change rules key off. Vue's Toolbar renders ReviewControls.vue (same track-changes toggle + display-mode selector) gated on `showReviewControls` (default true), the toggle emits through `setEditorMode(toggledTrackChangesMode(...))` into the same core `setCanonicalMode` path, and the selector sets a local `displayMode` that DocxEditor.vue applies as the identical `folio-root--<mode>` class, with the same tracked-change display CSS ported verbatim into a non-scoped style block. Divergence: Vue additionally keeps its EditingModeDropdown (a Vue-only three-mode editing/suggesting/viewing picker React lacks), so `viewing` stays reachable there; the toggle itself only flips editing<->suggesting, matching React exactly. Vue holds `displayMode` in a local ref rather than core's EditorModeManager (which React binds via useEditorMode), same observable behavior.
pairedNotes.toolbarExtra: Different-idiom match, both wired. React renders the `toolbarExtra` ReactNode as FormattingBar children (`toolbarChildren = toolbarExtra ?? null`). Vue renders the `toolbarExtra` VNodeChild prop into the toolbar's `#toolbar-extra` outlet via VNodeRenderer, with a host-provided `#toolbar-extra` slot taking precedence. Same capability (inject custom toolbar content); the prop is now functional in Vue, not just the slot.

ref.comment: DocxEditorRef parity. Both adapters declare an identical DocxEditorRef type surface (Vue's assembled object `satisfies DocxEditorRef`). `paired` members have a real implementation in useDocxEditorRefApi.ts; `deferredInVue` members are stubbed to a constant (null / false / [] / no-op) with a PORT-BLOCKED note in that file, pending the backing composable/component.

pairedNotes.applyDocumentOperations: Both assert the batch version (`assertSupportedFolioDocumentOperationVersion`), return an all-skipped `unsupportedBlock` result at the contract version when no view or canonical session is mounted, and otherwise delegate to the canonical session's `applyCanonicalDocumentOperations` with the same snapshot/batch/author. A committed suggested batch is recorded in the pending-suggestion registry against the suggestions active before it, so hosts export and restore it like any other.
pairedNotes.hasPendingChanges: Both report pending document edits and comment mutations. A successful host-facing save clears the document signal when the serialized snapshot is still current and clears the comment signal. Document load resets both signals. Controller serialization via getEditor().getDocx() leaves both signals intact. React reads the canonical session journal and its comment dirty flag. Vue reads isDirty from useDocxEditor and commentsDirty from useCommentManagement. Both return false before the editor view mounts.
pairedNotes.openFind: Both open the adapter's find surface. React reuses the shortcut path: the same selection seed (readFindSelectionSeed) and the same dialog-state opener the Cmd/Ctrl+F handler calls. Vue's find/replace panel has a single open state and no selection seeding, so openFind sets showFindReplace; the search box starts from its own last value.
pairedNotes.openReplace: Both open the adapter's find surface in replace intent. React opens the dialog's replace mode with the same selection seed as openFind. Vue's panel has one open state with the replace row behind its own toggle, so this opens the same panel as openFind.
pairedNotes.getEditorRef: Both wired with live handles. Vue synthesizes the PagedEditorRef shape from the shared controller and viewport primitives; getHfView delegates to the same relationship-id-keyed persistent header/footer manager that supplies the Vue layout pipeline, matching React's manager-backed lookup. Focus and history resolve the live active story; body selection, dispatch, layout, scroll, and page methods remain direct controller bindings. ensureView accepts the parity {focus} option while the shared controller currently treats creation and focus as separate operations.

pagedRef.comment: Nested PagedEditorRef parity. Both adapters expose this handle through DocxEditorRef.getEditorRef(); every paired method must be implemented on both sides.
